wa_right_cliff.blurb: Right Cliff is a small bouldering wall in the north Okanogan, part of the Clown Show Circuit near Tonasket. It sits at the far right end of that circuit, with the main face tucked uphill among trees, and a smaller upper wall above it. The gneiss here is on the steep side and the landings are friendly, which suits newer boulderers. Fifteen short problems run from the easiest grade up to about V1, so it is a place for mellow mileage, not hard sending. At least one line is on a shaded face, so expect cool conditions.

wa_rosario_beach_refrigerator_wall.blurb: A small bolted wall beside Rosario Beach at Deception Pass, on the west side of Fidalgo Island. The face is slightly overhanging with low texture, so the climbing is powerful and sequence-driven. Most of the fifteen lines are sport routes, mostly in the 5.11 to 5.13 range with a single 5.10, plus one trad line and a V4 traverse. Because of the lean it is reported to stay dry in light rain, and it picks up filtered sun late in the afternoon and evening. Not a place for beginners, but a handy short session for strong climbers.

wa_we_did_rock.blurb: We Did Rock is a sport crag in the Deception Crags group at Exit 38 near North Bend, reached along the old railroad grade just east of Deception Wall. The cliff is split, with a tall grippy slab on one side and a steeper blocky face on the other. Its fifteen routes are mostly in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, with a couple of easier lines and two near 5.12, so it is the place to come for moderates. Routes face north to northeast, catching sun through the late morning before trees shade them around midday. It is among the busier walls here.

wa_peannacle_point.blurb: Peannacle Point is one of the crags in Bob's Area, a subalpine cluster above Exit 38 in the Mount Washington crags near North Bend. Most of its fifteen routes are bolted, with two trad lines, and the grades lean moderate: a large share sit around 5.8 to 5.10, with one at 5.11. That makes it a good stop for newer leaders and for warming up before steeper walls nearby. Climbers mention broad views along the valley from the face. The rock at the neighbouring crags in the area is considered some of the best at Exit 38.

wa_duck_wall.blurb: Duck Wall is a crag above the town of Index, in the Lookout Point area, just left of the main Lookout Point cliff. The main section is a white face visible from town, topped by a large left-facing roof, and it is steeper than Lookout Point though not quite vertical. Lower tiers hold short crack climbs. Most of the fifteen routes are trad, with a few sport lines, a boulder problem and a top rope, spanning roughly 5.8 to 5.13.

wa_julia_s_outcrop.blurb: Julia's Outcrop is a small overhanging sandstone cliff perched above Chuckanut Drive south of Bellingham. Routes are short, roughly 30 to 70 feet, with a mix of sport and trad lines from easy 5.5 up to about 5.12, and the bulk sit near 5.9. The rock is soft, so it needs a couple of dry days after rain. Several lines were re-bolted with glue-ins in 2022, but older bolts can be widely spaced and the first clip is high on some routes. The walk up is short but steep, with a fixed rope.

wa_5_star_boulder.blurb: The Five Star Boulder is one of the best-known blocks in the Gold Bar bouldering zone, found along Reiter Road between Gold Bar and Index in the Skykomish Valley. It is a short hike from the road. Fifteen problems cover a very wide range, from an easy V0 up through the mid grades and on to a handful of hard V10 to V13 lines. The rock is Gold Bar granite, and the boulder is often described as the finest in the state.
